paragraphs: Neuro-symbolic systems combine learned concepts with symbolic reasoning. A central question is whether solving the overall task provides enough information to learn the intended concepts. This paper develops a theoretical account of that question by translating neuro-symbolic tasks into derived constraint satisfaction problems, or DCSPs. These problems describe the solutions compatible with a task's constraints.

Within the paper's framework, a task is learnable exactly when its DCSP has a unique solution. This connects learning to ambiguity: multiple compatible solutions can leave the intended concepts unresolved. Under mild assumptions, the authors also establish sample complexity for learnable tasks, characterizing how much data learning requires.

For general tasks, the analysis connects asymptotic expected concept error to how much the DCSP solutions disagree. This gives reasoning shortcuts and learnability a shared explanation: successful reasoning can coexist with ambiguous underlying concepts. The contribution is a principled way to examine whether a task's constraints identify the intended solution and to guide the design of neuro-symbolic systems accordingly.
neurips-2025-a-learnability-analysis-on-.tldr: The paper characterizes neuro-symbolic learnability through constraint-solution uniqueness and links concept errors to disagreement among compatible solutions.

paragraphs: Digital twins of visual cortex are neural networks trained to predict brain responses to images. Predicting individual neurons accurately, however, does not establish that a model captures how groups of neurons represent objects. This paper examines whether these models reproduce changes across the visual hierarchy, especially the ability to recognize objects despite changes in appearance.

The authors find that existing models capture hierarchical changes in basic neuron properties, including receptive field size, but miss more complex population representations. They introduce a hierarchical readout inspired by cortical anatomy. Each visual area receives a projection from a different depth of one shared network, connecting cortical hierarchy to the model's internal hierarchy.

This arrangement improves predictions of how population representations transform across areas. It outperforms readouts using only the final layer and alternatives that change architecture, regularization, or training loss. The findings suggest that anatomical structure supplies a useful learning bias, helping digital twins capture aspects of brain computation that accurate individual-neuron predictions alone can overlook.
neurips-2025-anatomically-inspired-digit.tldr: Connecting visual areas to different network depths helps digital twins reproduce hierarchical population representations of objects.

paragraphs: Flow matching generates data by learning a trajectory from noise to a finished sample. A common design uses one large network throughout this trajectory, repeatedly evaluating it during generation. The paper argues that this makes one model responsible for different signal characteristics at different times while also creating substantial inference costs.

Blockwise Flow Matching divides the trajectory into time intervals and assigns a smaller, specialized velocity block to each interval. Each block learns the transformation needed in its own part of generation. A Semantic Feature Guidance module supplies meaningful features aligned with pretrained representations, helping guide these transformations toward higher-quality outputs.

The framework also includes Feature Residual Approximation, a lightweight strategy intended to retain semantic quality while reducing inference cost. On ImageNet at 256 by 256 resolution, the authors report an improved tradeoff between generation quality and computational expense. At comparable generation performance, inference complexity improves by factors of 2.1 to 4.9. These results support dividing generative work among specialized blocks rather than repeatedly assigning every stage to the same large network.
neurips-2025-blockwise-flow-matching-imp.tldr: Specialized blocks for different generation intervals improve flow matching's quality–compute tradeoff, with reported inference-complexity gains of 2.1–4.9 times.

paragraphs: A neural network can be fingerprinted through its responses to selected inputs, called triggers. This allows model copyright tracing even when only input-output access is available. The challenge becomes harder when many candidate models must be distinguished using few queries, because querying the service carries a cost.

This paper studies fingerprints through information theory. Instead of evaluating only whether a fingerprint remains robust, it asks how informative each trigger is for identifying the model. The proposed principle selects triggers with the largest marginal mutual information: inputs whose responses add the most identifying information beyond what other triggers already provide.

The authors show that this selection principle can make tracing both more accurate and more query-efficient. Their experiments support incorporating the method into existing fingerprinting schemes. The contribution therefore concerns how fingerprint queries are chosen, rather than replacing the overall idea of identifying networks by their outputs. It brings the distinctiveness of a fingerprint across many models into the same discussion as its robustness.
neurips-2025-boosting-the-uniqueness-of-.tldr: Selecting fingerprint triggers by their added identifying information improves neural-network copyright tracing accuracy and query efficiency.

paragraphs: Language-model cascades reduce reasoning costs by sending easier queries to inexpensive models and escalating harder ones to stronger models. Choosing when to escalate is difficult: a cascade should preserve answer quality while keeping spending under control. C3PO addresses this routing problem without requiring labeled examples of correct answers.

The framework optimizes regret relative to the most powerful model, using unlabeled model outputs to construct the cascade. It combines this objective with conformal prediction to bound the probability that inference cost exceeds a user-selected budget. This is probabilistic cost control, so the guarantee concerns how often the budget may be exceeded rather than imposing a hard ceiling on every query.

The authors provide theoretical guarantees for cost control and generalization error, and report effective optimization with small calibration sets. Across GSM8K, MATH-500, BigBench-Hard, and AIME, C3PO outperforms strong cascade baselines in accuracy and cost-efficiency. The findings support using a powerful model as a reference for label-free cascade optimization while giving users a principled way to manage computational risk.
neurips-2025-c3po-optimized-large-langua.tldr: C3PO learns language-model cascades without labeled answers while bounding the probability of exceeding a chosen inference budget.

paragraphs: Video super-resolution aims to restore higher-resolution video from degraded input. Diffusion models offer promising restoration quality, but repeatedly sampling over dozens of steps makes them slow. DOVE targets single-step restoration, addressing the difficulty of achieving sufficient fidelity while managing the expense of training on video.

The method adapts the pretrained CogVideoX video diffusion model through fine-tuning. Its latent-pixel training strategy uses two stages to gradually adapt the model to super-resolution. The authors also build a video processing pipeline that produces HQ-VSR, a high-quality dataset designed for this task. Fine-tuning on that dataset further improves the model's restoration capability.

Experiments find that DOVE achieves comparable or better performance than diffusion-based video super-resolution methods that use multiple sampling steps. The authors report inference speedups of up to 28 times over existing methods such as MGLD-VSR. The result shows that, in the evaluated settings, adapting a pretrained video model through targeted training and data construction can substantially reduce sampling work while preserving competitive restoration quality.
neurips-2025-dove-efficient-one-step-dif.tldr: DOVE adapts a pretrained video diffusion model for competitive single-step super-resolution, reporting speedups of up to 28 times.

paragraphs: Zeroth-order optimization works from function evaluations rather than directly supplied gradients. This paper develops quantum methods that estimate gradients or subgradients using noisy function-evaluation access. It studies both smooth convex objectives and nonsmooth ones, where ordinary gradients may not exist everywhere.

The main result is query complexity that is independent of dimension apart from polylogarithmic factors. Using only noisy function values, the methods match the first-order query complexity of classical gradient descent. The authors establish an exponential separation between quantum and classical zeroth-order optimization. This comparison concerns oracle queries, the calls made to obtain function information.

The authors also extend quantum gradient estimation to non-Euclidean optimization through mirror descent, dual averaging, and mirror prox. Connecting semidefinite programming with eigenvalue optimization yields algorithms for semidefinite programs, linear programs, and zero-sum games. For zero-sum games, they identify a parameter regime where their algorithm is faster than existing classical and quantum approaches. The result is explicitly tied to that regime, rather than asserting an advantage for every game.
neurips-2025-fast-zeroth-order-convex-op.tldr: Quantum gradient estimation enables nearly dimension-independent query complexity for convex optimization using noisy function values.

paragraphs: Stochastic gradient descent uses noisy updates, so understanding its behavior requires more than locating a target point. This paper studies the fluctuations around that target when the learning rate remains constant. It develops both asymptotic results and finite-sample guarantees, linking long-run distributional behavior to bounds that apply before an infinite-data limit.

A new linear approximation technique establishes a quenched central limit theorem with refined tail properties. Under the paper's conditions, the fluctuations converge to a multivariate normal distribution regardless of initialization. The authors describe their conditions as substantially milder than those of classical SGD central limit theorems while obtaining a stronger convergence result.

The analysis also supplies a Berry–Esseen bound, which quantifies Gaussian approximation error for constant-rate SGD. An autoregressive approximation produces a Nagaev-type inequality controlling tail probabilities and giving non-asymptotic large-deviation guarantees. Numerical simulations verify the results. Together, these contributions provide foundations for uncertainty quantification that addresses both the accuracy of a Gaussian approximation and the possibility of unusually large deviations.
neurips-2025-gaussian-approximation-and-.tldr: The paper establishes Gaussian approximation and tail bounds for constant-learning-rate SGD, supporting uncertainty quantification at finite sample sizes.

paragraphs: Image segmentation can admit several plausible answers because boundaries are uncertain and annotators disagree. Returning only one segmentation hides that variability. This paper develops a stochastic segmentation model that can represent multiple possibilities while making its internal representation more expressive and interpretable.

The framework combines a conditional variational autoencoder with a Gaussian mixture model and a normalizing flow. The mixture organizes the latent space into meaningful semantic clusters, while the flow captures feature deformations together with quantified uncertainty. Constraints on latent means and variances stabilize these distributions. This responds partly to the authors' observation that models such as Probabilistic U-Net can rely excessively on high latent variance, leading to posterior collapse.

The authors evaluate the approach on LIDC, Crack500, and Cityscapes, reporting improvements over state-of-the-art methods in curvilinear structure and medical image segmentation. The contribution is a structured way to represent segmentation alternatives: semantic grouping and flexible deformation modeling serve different roles. The findings support this combination as a way to improve stochastic segmentation beyond simply increasing variability in the latent representation.
neurips-2025-gmm-based-vae-model-with-no.tldr: Combining clustered latent representations with normalizing flows improves stochastic segmentation while constraining unstable latent variability.

paragraphs: Personalizing generated content requires learning what a particular user prefers. Existing approaches can demand many preference questions or require users to express their preferences directly in text. UserAlign instead asks for a few comparisons between pairs of responses and uses those choices to select a personalized output at inference time.

The method builds on best-arm identification in logistic bandits, a framework for finding the best candidate through informative feedback. Its candidates form a fixed pool of responses already generated by the model. UserAlign incorporates the assumption that the user's feedback is consistent and noise-free to identify the preferred response quickly.

That assumption is central to how the method uses a small number of comparisons, and the selected answer is limited to the available response pool. Experiments across personalized text and image generation tasks demonstrate the method's effectiveness. The contribution is a way to turn lightweight comparative feedback into response selection, reducing the need for either extensive questioning or an explicit written description of the user's preferences.
neurips-2025-inference-time-personalized.tldr: UserAlign selects personalized responses from a fixed candidate pool using a few pairwise comparisons under consistent, noise-free feedback.

paragraphs: Long-term forecasting can benefit from patterns that recur across periods. MoFo approaches periodicity through two complementary relationships: correlations between time steps occupying the same position in different periods, and trends between different positions within a period. Its representation and attention mechanism are designed around these relationships.

The model constructs two-dimensional patches through discrete sampling. Rows contain period-aligned time steps, making their correlations directly accessible, while columns align steps at different offsets within a period. A period-aware modulator then encourages attention coefficients to follow periodic trends. It does this through a regulated relaxation function that supplies an adaptive learning bias.

Because that function is trained end to end, the periodic bias can adapt to different datasets instead of remaining entirely fixed. Benchmark experiments show competitive forecasting performance alongside high memory efficiency and fast training. The paper's contribution is therefore both representational and architectural: it reorganizes observations to expose recurring structure and guides attention toward that structure, helping the model capture the periodic patterns relevant to long-term predictions.
neurips-2025-mofo-empowering-long-term-t.tldr: MoFo combines period-structured inputs with adaptive attention guidance to forecast recurring patterns efficiently.

paragraphs: Multi-objective reinforcement learning must account for several goals that may compete. Under a max-min criterion, the policy seeks to improve its worst-performing objective. This paper develops a practical framework for that criterion by recasting the learning problem as a regularized, continuous two-player zero-sum game.

The authors introduce a mirror-descent algorithm for the reformulated problem. It simplifies policy updates while providing global last-iterate convergence, meaning the convergence guarantee applies to the latest iterate itself. The theoretical analysis covers iteration complexity with both exact and approximate policy evaluations, as well as sample complexity bounds.

An additional version uses adaptive regularization to improve performance. Experiments demonstrate the algorithm's convergence behavior in tabular settings, and a deep reinforcement learning implementation significantly outperforms previous baselines in many multi-objective environments. The work combines a game-theoretic formulation with an algorithm that has convergence guarantees and an empirical implementation for more complex settings. Its theoretical and experimental contributions jointly support the approach to balancing objectives through the max-min criterion.
neurips-2025-multi-objective-reinforceme.tldr: A game-theoretic mirror-descent framework provides last-iterate convergence for max-min multi-objective reinforcement learning and strong empirical results.

paragraphs: Entropy calibration asks whether a language model's uncertainty over its generated text matches its log loss on human text. Earlier findings show growing entropy and declining text quality during longer generations. Truncating the sampling distribution can improve quality, but sacrifices diversity and increases log loss. This paper asks whether scale resolves the problem and whether calibration can avoid that tradeoff.

In a simplified theoretical setting, the rate at which miscalibration improves with dataset size depends on the data distribution's power-law exponent. When that exponent is near one, improvement is extremely slow. Measurements of language models from 0.5 billion to 70 billion parameters show similarly small fitted scaling exponents, with larger models accumulating error at rates similar to smaller ones.

These results offer one explanation for why larger models still use substantial sampling truncation despite producing better text. The authors also prove that entropy can be reduced while preserving log loss, conditional on access to a black box capable of fitting predictors of future text entropy. That establishes a theoretical possibility under a specific assumption.
neurips-2025-on-the-entropy-calibration-.tldr: Entropy miscalibration improves slowly with scale, but reducing entropy without worsening log loss is theoretically possible under a future-entropy prediction assumption.

paragraphs: Online inverse linear optimization learns an agent's linear objective by observing its choices from changing feasible sets. Prediction quality is measured through regret: the accumulated objective-value gap caused by following the learner's predictions. Earlier logarithmic-regret methods maintained possible-objective regions with a number of constraints growing with the time horizon, making long runs computationally expensive.

The paper applies online Newton step to suitable exp-concave losses. It achieves the best-known regret order, O(n ln T), while making per-round complexity independent of the horizon T; n is the objective-vector dimension. The main advance is retaining a strong regret guarantee without the growing constraint-maintenance burden.

The authors also address agents that sometimes choose suboptimally. Using MetaGrad, which runs online Newton step at multiple learning rates, they obtain regret O(n ln T + sqrt(Δ_T n ln T)), where Δ_T measures cumulative agent suboptimality. Finally, a lower bound of Ω(n) shows that the optimal-action guarantee is tight up to a logarithmic factor. These results connect computational efficiency with quantified robustness to imperfect observed decisions.
neurips-2025-online-inverse-linear-optim.tldr: An online Newton method achieves logarithmic regret for inverse linear optimization without per-round complexity growing with the time horizon.

paragraphs: Contextual sparsity accelerates language models by activating only some parameters for each token. Its benefit can disappear when many tokens are processed together: their different active neurons collectively cover nearly the full model. Polar Sparsity examines how this problem changes across model components as batch size and sequence length increase.

The authors identify a shift from feed-forward MLP layers toward attention. Batching makes MLP computation more efficient while eroding its sparsity. Attention, meanwhile, becomes increasingly expensive, but sparsity among attention heads remains stable across batch sizes. The proposed Selective Head Attention mechanism targets this opportunity, supported by GPU kernels designed to execute sparse attention efficiently.

Across models including OPT, LLaMA-2 and 3, Qwen, and Mistral, the authors report end-to-end speedups of up to 2.2 times without compromising accuracy. The experiments cover varied batch sizes and sequence lengths. The contribution is evidence that contextual sparsity can remain useful for high-throughput inference when the sparsity mechanism and hardware implementation focus on attention heads rather than relying on MLP sparsity alone.
neurips-2025-polar-sparsity-high-through.tldr: Polar Sparsity targets attention heads to preserve contextual-sparsity benefits in batched inference, reporting up to 2.2-times end-to-end speedups.

paragraphs: Hypothesis selection asks which candidate probability distribution best matches the distribution that produced observed samples. This paper studies the task under local differential privacy, where queries to individuals must satisfy privacy constraints. Given k candidates, the goal is to return one nearly as close to the underlying distribution as the best available candidate.

The proposed algorithm uses approximately k to the three-halves non-adaptive queries, with logarithmic factors suppressed. Non-adaptive queries can be specified without choosing later questions based on earlier answers. Previous approaches required either at least quadratic query counts or many rounds of interactive querying, creating a tradeoff between query volume and interaction.

The technical tool is the Scheffé graph, which records structure in the differences between candidate distributions. Using that structure enables the improved query bound while retaining local privacy and near-best hypothesis selection. The authors suggest that this graph may also prove useful for other hypothesis-selection tasks. That broader relevance remains a possibility, while the demonstrated contribution is the more query-efficient, non-adaptive private selection algorithm.
neurips-2025-query-efficient-locally-pri.tldr: The Scheffé graph enables locally private hypothesis selection with roughly k to the three-halves non-adaptive queries.

paragraphs: Language models can influence human decisions even when their answers are confidently wrong. Retrieval-augmented generation brings external documents into response generation to improve the information available to the model. This paper argues that retrieving documents primarily for relevance leaves another important objective insufficiently addressed: how well calibrated the resulting human decisions are.

CalibRAG introduces a retrieval method explicitly oriented toward calibration. In this setting, the concern is whether confidence in decisions informed by the generated response fits their reliability. The approach therefore evaluates the role of retrieved evidence through its contribution to decision-making, extending the aim beyond selecting documents closely related to the original query.

Across multiple datasets, the authors find that CalibRAG improves both calibration and accuracy relative to comparison methods. Those findings support treating calibration as a retrieval objective alongside the usefulness of evidence for answering a question. The central contribution is connecting document retrieval to the reliability of downstream decisions, with empirical results indicating that improved calibration can accompany improved accuracy in the evaluated tasks.
neurips-2025-reliable-decisionmaking-via.tldr: CalibRAG retrieves evidence with decision calibration in mind, improving both calibration and accuracy across evaluated datasets.

paragraphs: Predicting human movement requires tracking both long-range dependencies and recurring patterns at different time scales. RHYTHM uses a large language model as a spatial and temporal predictor, organizing movement histories so that daily and weekly structure remains accessible without processing an unnecessarily long sequence.

The framework partitions trajectories into daily segments and represents them as discrete tokens. Hierarchical attention captures dependencies at daily and weekly scales; the authors describe this tokenization as quadratically reducing sequence length while preserving cyclical information. Precomputed prompt embeddings for trajectory segments and prediction targets enrich these tokens before they enter the language-model backbone.

The pretrained backbone remains frozen, reducing training time and memory use while the framework adapts its representations around it. Evaluation against state-of-the-art methods on three real-world datasets shows reported improvements of 2.4% in overall accuracy and 5.0% on weekends, alongside a 24.6% reduction in training time. These findings support matching the input representation to mobility's temporal rhythms when adapting a language model to trajectory prediction.
neurips-2025-rhythm-reasoning-with-hiera.tldr: RHYTHM combines daily trajectory tokens, hierarchical attention, and a frozen language model to improve mobility prediction and training efficiency.

paragraphs: Text-to-image models can depict the right objects while reversing who performs an action. RoleBench measures this problem using action-based relations, such as a mouse chasing a cat. The authors find that leading models and compositional generation methods often fall back to the more familiar reversed relation, a failure they call role collapse.

Their analysis shows that models may fail on a rare relation yet succeed on related intermediate compositions. This suggests that frequent reversed counterparts contribute to the problem, alongside any shortage of rare examples. Based on that observation, the authors hypothesize that teaching directional relationships through intermediate compositions can reduce role collapse.

ReBind tests this idea through lightweight fine-tuning on carefully selected active and passive intermediate compositions. Experiments suggest substantial reductions in role collapse, with human evaluators preferring ReBind over state-of-the-art methods more than 78% of the time. The findings highlight asymmetry between common and uncommon relations as a contributor to compositional failure and support intermediate role-binding examples as a practical mitigation.
neurips-2025-role-bias-in-diffusion-mode.tldr: RoleBench exposes action-role reversals in image generation, and ReBind reduces them through fine-tuning on intermediate compositions.

paragraphs: Learning to align 3D point clouds with text is constrained by the scarcity of large paired datasets. SceneForge expands training data by assembling individual 3D shapes into scenes containing multiple objects with explicit spatial relationships. It pairs these scenes with coherent descriptions refined by a large language model.

These compositions add relational structure and diversity to contrastive training. The authors investigate how many objects to include, how frequently compositional examples should appear in training batches, and how scenes should be constructed. The augmentations work across encoder architectures, so the approach can improve multiple models through the training examples they receive.

Experiments report substantial gains in zero-shot classification across ModelNet, ScanObjNN, Objaverse-LVIS, and ScanNet, plus few-shot part segmentation on ShapeNetPart. SceneForge also improves visual question answering on ScanQA and generalizes robustly in retrieval as scenes become more complex. Demonstrations of adapting spatial configurations to textual instructions further support its spatial reasoning capabilities. Together, the results show how structured scene composition can strengthen both object recognition and the connection between language and spatial arrangements.
neurips-2025-sceneforge-enhancing-3d-tex.tldr: SceneForge improves 3D–text learning by augmenting training with multi-object scenes and descriptions that explicitly encode spatial relationships.

paragraphs: Detecting anomalies across several time-varying signals is difficult when abnormal examples are scarce and relationships between variables change. Reconstruction-based methods can also become so focused on normal patterns that subtle anomalies receive insufficient attention. SPAGD addresses these issues by combining generated training signals with a graph that responds to potential disruptions.

A self-perturbation module creates altered time series through the reconstruction process applied to normal data. These auxiliary examples help alleviate the imbalance between normal and anomalous training signals. Their reconstruction residuals then guide an anomaly-aware graph module, which dynamically adjusts connections to emphasize disruptions in relationships between variables.

A detection module combines spatial and temporal convolutions to distinguish normal sequences from the self-perturbed examples. This connects the generated training signals to both graph construction and classification, allowing the model to learn from candidate disruptions rather than only reconstructing normality. Experiments across multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate effectiveness relative to state-of-the-art baselines. The contribution is an integrated approach to scarce anomaly examples and changing inter-variable structure.
neurips-2025-self-perturbed-anomaly-awar.tldr: SPAGD uses self-perturbed sequences and dynamically adjusted variable relationships to improve multivariate time-series anomaly detection.

paragraphs: A multi-objective contextual bandit repeatedly chooses actions while learning about several potentially conflicting rewards. The challenge is to explore uncertain actions without consistently making poor tradeoffs. This paper introduces MOL-TS, a Thompson Sampling algorithm with Pareto regret guarantees for the setting where rewards depend linearly on contextual features.

MOL-TS samples parameters across objectives and chooses an action from an effective Pareto front. Unlike approaches that recompute an empirical Pareto front each round, this construction accounts for repeated selections over time. The design combines randomized exploration with an efficient way to handle tradeoffs among multiple objectives.

The authors establish a worst-case Pareto regret bound of approximately d to the three-halves times the square root of T, suppressing logarithmic factors. Here d is feature dimension and T is the number of rounds. This matches the best-known order for randomized linear bandit algorithms with one objective. Empirical results show improved regret minimization and strong multi-objective performance, supporting the algorithm's ability to manage competing objectives without worsening that known regret order.
neurips-2025-thompson-sampling-for-multi.tldr: MOL-TS provides Thompson Sampling with Pareto regret guarantees for linear contextual bandits with competing objectives.

paragraphs: Visual place recognition compares images through compact global descriptors. A common pipeline first extracts local patch features and then uses a dedicated aggregator to combine them. This paper investigates whether a transformer backbone can perform that aggregation internally through its existing self-attention mechanism.

The method inserts learnable aggregation tokens before a selected transformer block. These tokens interact globally with image patch tokens as the network processes them, gathering useful information. At the final output, the aggregation tokens are concatenated into the image descriptor. The authors also study insertion and initialization choices empirically and propose strategies based on those findings.

Experiments show stronger performance than state-of-the-art methods on several place-recognition datasets, with higher efficiency and a reported first-place ranking on the MSLS challenge leaderboard. The contribution is a simple representation design that integrates aggregation into the backbone. Its success supports using transformer token interactions to construct robust global descriptors, while the empirical studies address the practical choices needed to make that mechanism effective.
neurips-2025-towards-implicit-aggregatio.tldr: Learnable tokens let a transformer aggregate image information internally, improving place-recognition accuracy and efficiency.

paragraphs: Using more computation at inference time can improve language-model reasoning, but how that computation is allocated matters. This paper trains a value model to guide the search through long reasoning traces. Its training method avoids requiring a precise division into reasoning steps, which can be difficult to define for long-context models.

The authors collect 2.5 million reasoning traces and train a 1.5-billion-parameter value model that operates at token level. They apply it to DeepSeek models through block-wise value-guided search. A final weighted majority vote combines the resulting answers, linking guidance during reasoning with aggregation at the end.

The experiments show better test-time scaling than majority voting and best-of-n methods. Value-guided search also substantially reduces the inference FLOPs needed to match majority voting's performance. This indicates that the learned value estimates help use computation more effectively than the compared approaches. The authors release the dataset, model, and codebase, making both the training resources and the search method available for further work.
neurips-2025-value-guided-search-for-eff.tldr: A token-level value model guides block-wise reasoning search, improving test-time scaling and reducing compute relative to majority voting.

paragraphs: Inverse folding models have become effective zero-shot predictors of protein stability, but their success leaves a conceptual question. How do the amino-acid preferences expressed by these models relate to the free-energy considerations that govern thermodynamic stability? This paper develops that connection to better understand existing predictions and identify ways to improve them.

The authors derive a free-energy interpretation of inverse folding models. Their analysis shows that the commonly used likelihood-ratio approach is a simplified approximation. It also suggests several alternative paths for estimating relative stability more accurately, turning the theoretical interpretation into changes that can be assessed empirically.

The authors evaluate these approaches and report considerable improvements in zero-shot performance using fairly simple means. The contribution therefore combines explanation with practical prediction gains: understanding what a model-derived score approximates can help improve the score itself. The results support refining how inverse folding outputs are translated into stability estimates, while the theoretical work takes steps toward clarifying the physical foundations of those estimates.
neurips-2025-zero-shot-protein-stability.tldr: A free-energy interpretation reveals approximations in inverse-folding stability scores and motivates simple changes that improve zero-shot prediction.
